result:
I added the token count to the client list and a new endpoint that revokes all of a client's tokens. I did not run tests, lint, typecheck or the app, as you asked. I also wrote no tests.

**List count.** Each client in `GET /mcp/oauth-clients` now has `activeAccessTokens`.
- **Per consent row.** The list has one row per client and consenting user. The count is for that user's tokens on that client. In the `ownership=all` view, each owner's row has its own count.
- **How "valid" is decided.** Access token rows store no expiry, so I read the `exp` claim from each stored JWT without verifying it, and count only tokens that have not expired. The value is for display only. The lookup is one query per page, not one per client.

**New endpoint.** `POST /mcp/oauth-clients/:clientId/revoke-tokens` deletes every access and refresh token of that client, for all users.
- It needs the `mcp:manage` scope and returns 404 for an unknown client.
- The client, its consents and its authorization codes stay.
- Users can authorize the client again.
- Unlike the existing delete route, it sends no email to the affected users.

**Files changed.**
- `packages/@n8n/api-types/src/dto/oauth/oauth-client.dto.ts`: the new count field and `RevokeOAuthClientTokensResponseDto`.
- `packages/cli/src/modules/oauth-server/oauth-clients.controller.ts`: maps the count into the list response and adds the endpoint.
- `packages/cli/src/modules/oauth-server/oauth-server.service.ts`: adds the count to each client and a `revokeClientTokens` method.
- `packages/cli/src/modules/oauth-server/oauth-token.service.ts`: counts unexpired access tokens per user and client and revokes all tokens of a client.
- `packages/cli/src/modules/oauth-server/database/repositories/oauth-access-token.repository.ts`: finds tokens for a set of clients and users and deletes all tokens of a client.
- `packages/cli/src/modules/oauth-server/database/repositories/oauth-refresh-token.repository.ts`: deletes all refresh tokens of a client.

`activeAccessTokens` is now required on the list response type. A last grep for other users of that type failed on a shell glob, so I did not confirm that nothing else (tests, frontend) builds it. Typecheck will show any that do.
